Presidents’ Day originally began as a way to honor George Washington, and in 1879 it became a national holiday when President Rutherford B. Hayes signed it into law, recognizing the importance of leadership rooted in service, not power.

In 1971, under President Richard Nixon, the holiday was moved to the third Monday in February through the Uniform Monday Holiday Act. While the official name remains Washington’s Birthday, the day became widely known as Presidents’ Day, reflecting a broader idea: honoring not just one president, but the institution itself.

That shift mattered. It acknowledged that the presidency carries enormous responsibility and that the American people place real faith in this office to lead with integrity, protect our democracy, and serve the common good.

Today, as the President constantly tests the boundaries of the office and uses it for personal gain—from a $400 million Qatari jet, to $500 million of foreign investment into his crypto company in exchange for access to AI chips—let us resolve to elect a Congress willing to stand up to him as the coequal branch of government that the Constitution requires them to be.

#PresidentsDay #GeorgeWashington #History
Arizona is 30 years into a drought and bracing for deeper Colorado River cuts. Jay Feely's plan? More data centers in the desert. It's disqualifying.

I'm squarely on the side of AI safety. Human dignity and human safety is non-negotiable, as far as I'm concerned. AI has the potential in the future to provide benefits, but we have to make sure that any technology that we use has to be used responsibly.

We are here in the desert, running out of water. The Trump administration cut our allocation recently, and he wants to put data centers into CD 1. Not on my watch. You're not going to put a bunch of data centers here to chew up more of our water, which is just going to hit people in the pocketbook.
We can't have them here in our district. We can have them in other places in America where they have an abundance of water, which we don't have here.
AI is coming at us quick, and we are going to need data centers. I just don't want them in CD 1.
At that time, when we had those tax credits come up, AI wasn't on the radar.
